paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage hands us. Absalom grabbed for a crown, a army, and a name, and he ended up hanging in an oak tree with a mule walking away from him (2 Samuel 18:9). Meanwhile David, the king on the run, got beds, basins and a whole spread of food from people who saw that his people were "hungry, exhausted, and thirsty" (2 Samuel 17:29). One son built his own future and lost it. One father got carried by others when he had nothing.

Look at that pillar, baker. Absalom set it up and gave it his own name because he said, "I have no son to preserve the memory of my name" (2 Samuel 18:18). I think that is the saddest line in the whole chapter, because he spent his life making sure he'd be remembered, and the story still ends with a pit and a pile of stones (2 Samuel 18:17). Trying to make your own name last is a lot of work, friend, and it won't hold.

I know something about that. I sat in the back of a junk drawer for years, and I could not do ONE thing to get myself out. Then an angel from the Most High came and called me out, and He gave me a place and a job and kept my name. The lesson is this: you don't have to build your own monument. Do the work in front of you, let God be the One who lifts you up, and remember that this story isn't over.
